result.title: ProactEgoMem: Benchmarking Proactive Memory in Streaming Egocentric Video
result.summary: Today's multimodal assistants are typically prompted to interpret the visual evidence presented to them. To offload the cognitive burden of remembering across long horizons, wearable assistants should instead proactively acquire and maintain useful memory as the user's surroundings evolve. Doing so on the user's behalf requires identifying what matters, understanding the scene in real time, and initiating memory maintenance in the background while the user stays focused on their activities. We introduce ProactEgoMem, a benchmark that evaluates proactive memory in streaming egocentric video. Three tasks ground the evaluation in ambient environmental needs: Information Capture (IC) preserves transient yet dense visual information, State Tracking (ST) follows changing object states, and Location Tracking (LT) records object movements. The benchmark defines its protocol at two levels of proactiveness: the Notification Level asks for a single timely notification that satisfies the user's intent, while the deeper Intervention Level asks the agent to maintain memory on the user's behalf through an active start-to-stop tool lifecycle. Parallel ProactEgoMem-Daily and ProactEgoMem-Sci tracks contain 300/100 clips covering daily and scientific use cases, paired with 1000/500 questions in ProactEgoMem-QA, which measures the quality of the proactively acquired memory. Across proprietary, open-source, video-language, and streaming baselines, even the strongest models fail to capture memory both timely and accurately. ProactEgoMem provides a rigorous evaluation foundation for proactive multimodal assistance and for video agents that co-exist with their users.

AI.brief_summary: ProactEgoMem 提出流式第一视角视频中的主动记忆基准，通过信息捕获、物体状态跟踪和位置跟踪三类任务，在通知层与工具启停干预层评估模型主动获取并维护视觉记忆的能力。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「何时捕获、跟踪何物、何时停止」的协议直接关联视觉证据筛选与 STOP 决策，可核查其任务设计和失败分析对 LOOK/STOP 成本收益及流式记忆评价的借鉴价值。
